summary: The note describes how regional kitchens worldwide have adopted zero-waste cooking as of September 2023, using every edible part of ingredients while reviving traditional techniques. It profiles chefs in several cities who apply the approach to dishes, farm partnerships, education, economics, seasonality, heritage preservation and technology. It argues the movement is more than a trend, linking sustainability with economic viability, culinary heritage and community engagement.
one_line: Regional chefs worldwide are adopting zero-waste cooking, blending traditional frugality with modern innovation, farm partnerships, education, and sustainability recognition.
key_facts: Emilio Garcia of Barcelona showcased a Catalan dish on November 5, 2023, substituting the traditional seafood elements with by-products of the same ingredients.
Aisha Sullivan of New Orleans reintroduced a Creole vegetable dish on October 14, 2023, using stems and leaves that would typically not make it to the main course.
Chef Mei Lin of Vancouver and the Henderson Farm announced a collaboration on September 12, 2023, with farmers growing produce tailored to zero-waste programs, including carrot tops and beet leaves.
Chef Roberto Flores in Mexico City began a series of zero-waste workshops and cooking classes on September 25, 2023, teaching home cooks to shop wisely and use leftovers.
Chef Nadine Brown in Johannesburg debuted a zero-waste-focused menu on October 9, 2023, cutting waste removal and ingredient purchasing costs to offer dishes at more affordable prices.
Hiroshi Yamamoto of Kyoto curated a special winter menu on December 1, 2023, featuring daikon radishes using both the root and the green tops.
On September 8, 2023, a popular Michelin Guide incorporated a new rating system awarding additional recognition to restaurants excelling in zero-waste operations.
Chef Lola Martins in Lisbon has, since late 2023, advocated resurrecting old Portuguese culinary arts by integrating forgotten local ingredients and their full usage.
Chef Amar Shah launched the 'Global Local' campaign on November 22, 2023, to create a network of restaurants and kitchens committed to zero-waste practices.
Chef Sandra Lee in San Francisco released a dehydration device on October 17, 2023, turning surplus fruits and vegetable trimmings into shelf-stable garnishes and flavorings.
Zero-waste cooking is described as historically rooted in scarcity and frugality, when every edible part of food was used, a practice overshadowed by contemporary consumer culture.
